title: oekaki IR
description: The intermediate representation oekaki passes from parsers to renderers. Parsers produce it, enrichers annotate it, renderers consume it. Nothing else in the pipeline is load-bearing.

version.description: Schema version. Bumped when the shape changes incompatibly.

metadata.description: Provenance. Deliberately free of timestamps so that identical input yields byte-identical output.

generator.description: Tool and version that produced this document, e.g. "oekaki/0.2.0".

source.description: Parser that produced this document, e.g. "terraform".

source_version.description: Version of the upstream tool the input came from, e.g. a Terraform version.

scope.description: Names the estate this document describes, when ids have been qualified to be unique beyond one state file. A resource address is only unique within a single state, so `aws_vpc.main` from two teams' states are different VPCs; combining documents without a scope would silently merge them.

inputs.description: Repositories or documents selected for this graph, so downstream tools can distinguish available context from missing context.

source_version.description: Version of the source tool for this individual input, when inputs were combined from independently produced graphs.

overlays.description: The overlays applied to produce this document. Present so a reader can tell a purely derived graph from one carrying somebody's assertions.

axes.description: The ways this estate can be grouped. Infrastructure has no single correct hierarchy: the same database sits inside a subnet, inside an account, inside a module, and is owned by a team. Renderers nest by one axis at a time and leave the rest for colouring and filtering.

nodes.description: Resources drawn as boxes. Containers are not nodes; they appear in `groups`.

edges.description: Relationships drawn as arrows. The `kind` is the whole point of this schema.

groups.description: Containment, per axis. The authoritative record of parent/child nesting; the paths in a node's `groups` are built from these ids.

paths.description: Ordered walks through the estate: this one called that one, and that one called the next. An edge records one hop; a path records the order, which is what "this route has not been used in ninety days" and "this route fired when nothing declared it" are statements about. Kinds mean what they mean on an edge, so a declared path and an observed one can be compared.

observations.description: Time-scoped measurements and assessments attached to graph entities.

log_records.description: Classified log metadata only; raw log bodies are never stored in the graph.

log_status.description: Safe summary of the log polling component.

conflicts.description: Claims about the same thing that disagree. Recorded rather than resolved away: the document shows one value and admits it was contested, because a diagram that silently picks a winner is a diagram that lies quietly.

label.description: Human-readable name for a view selector.

id.description: Stable, human-greppable identity, unique across nodes AND groups, since an edge may point at either. The Terraform parser uses the resource address verbatim, e.g. "aws_ecs_service.api".

type.description: Provider resource type, e.g. "aws_ecs_service". Unrecognised types are legal and render as generic boxes.

description.description: Optional short explanation shown in interactive details.

provider.description: Short provider name, e.g. "aws" or "vsphere". Containment refuses to cross a boundary between two of these: referencing something is not the same as living inside it, and an on-premises machine that reads from a cloud database does not belong to that cloud's network.

groups.description: Maps an axis id to this node's group path on that axis, e.g. {"network": "aws_vpc.main/aws_subnet.private_a", "provider": "provider:aws"}. An axis absent here means the node sits at that axis's top level.

attrs.description: Attributes carried over from the source. Parsers own this.

metrics.description: Observed numbers. Enrichers own this; parsers must not write here.

from.description: Source id. May name a node or a group.

to.description: Target id. May name a node or a group: a reference to a container is a real dependency, and when containment cannot express it — across a provider boundary, say — an edge is the only honest way left to record it.

kind.description: iac_ref: one resource's configuration references another, so deleting the target breaks the source. reachable: the network permits this traffic. observed: this traffic actually happened.

relation.description: Open domain relationship vocabulary, such as calls, reads, writes, exposes, publishes, or contains. Kind remains the compatibility evidence category.

attrs.description: Kind-specific detail: the referencing attribute for iac_ref, the port range for reachable, the request rate for observed.

suppressed.description: Somebody asserted this edge is not real. A flag rather than a deletion, because "a human said this is wrong" and "this never existed" are different facts and only the first one is true.

id.description: Stable identity, unique across groups AND nodes. Must not contain a slash, since group paths are slash-separated.

axis.description: Which axis this container belongs to. A group's parent must be on the same axis.

label.description: Short label for the container's border.

parent.description: Enclosing group id, or null at top level.

nodes.description: The walk, in order. At least two participants, because one node is not a path, and they are node ids rather than group ids because a container does not call anything. A repeat is legal: a real request can come back through something it already went through.

kind.description: iac_ref: the configuration says this route exists. reachable: the network permits it. observed: something walked it. The gap between the first and the last is the whole point of recording paths.

claim.description: Who says so. Absent means a parser derived it from an input file, which is the overwhelmingly common case and therefore costs no bytes.

origin.description: parser: derived mechanically from an input file. human: entered by hand. ai: produced by a model. The three are kept apart because a diagram that cannot tell them apart presents somebody's guess with the authority of the code.

confidence.description: How sure the claimant is, 0..1. Absent means unstated, which is not the same as zero.

coverage.description: What is known about a node's log collection. Enrichers own this; parsers must not write here.

state.description: flowing: declared somewhere and something was seen. silent: declared, nothing seen. blind: somebody looked and found no destination. undeclared: logs arriving from something nothing declares. unknown: nobody asserted anything, or the assertion was ambiguous. Five states rather than four, because painting an unassessed resource as a blind spot is the same lie as painting a blind spot as covered.

reason.description: Why this state, in words a reader can argue with.

evidence.description: One declaration or observation. A coverage state with no evidence behind it is a conclusion with no basis, which is what this array exists to prevent.

kind.description: declared: configuration promises logs go here. observed: logs were actually seen here. none: somebody looked and found nothing, which is a finding rather than an absence.

sink.description: Id of the node logs go to.

records.description: How many were seen. Absent means no count was available, which is not the same as a count of zero.

via.description: How the claimant knew, in their own words.

matched.description: Which resolution rule tied this evidence to its node, so a surprising join can be traced without rerunning anything.

conflict.description: Two claims about the same thing that disagree.

target_kind.description: Discriminator for the target namespace. Entity ids are open strings and may resemble edge keys, so consumers must never infer this from target text.

target.description: A node or group id when target_kind is entity. For an edge, use `edge:` followed by four dot-separated components in from, to, kind, relation order. Each component is the RFC 4648 base64url encoding without padding of that string's UTF-8 bytes. The empty relation is still the fourth component, so a relation-less key ends in a dot. Example: from=a, to=b, kind=iac_ref, relation empty is `edge:YQ.Yg.aWFjX3JlZg.`.

claims.description: Every competing answer with its claimant, highest-ranked origin first. The first entry is the one the document displays.

overlayRef.description: An overlay that was applied to this document.

window.description: The period the overlay's author says their evidence covers, echoed verbatim. Nothing here is read from a clock, so determinism holds — and a diagram that says "blind spot" without saying over what period would be a lie of omission.

source.description: Where this came from in the original configuration, so a diagram can link back to code.
